court_name: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT BOMBAY
petitioner: Giri Textiles, through Proprietor Chandrayya R. Pasnuri
respondent: Anthony Nadar and Jainam Silk Mills
government_department_involved: Labour Court, Thane and Industrial Court, Thane

directives.text: Acknowledge receipt of the High Court's order dated April 30, 2026, dismissing the writ petition.
Forward the High Court's order to the Labour Court, Thane for further proceedings in Application (BIR) No. 1 of 2014.
Ensure Application (BIR) No. 1 of 2014 proceeds before the Labour Court, Thane on its merits, uninfluenced by previous observations except as concluded in the judgment.
Facilitate the Labour Court, Thane to decide Application (BIR) No. 1 of 2014, preferably within six months from the date of receipt of the High Court's order.
directives.deadline_text: Preferably within six months from receipt of order

directives.text: Record the dismissal of the writ petition and uphold the orders of the Labour Court and Industrial Court.
Discharge the rule and dispose of any pending interim applications as per the High Court's order.

raw_summary: The High Court dismissed the writ petition, upholding the orders of the Labour Court and Industrial Court. The petitioner's objection regarding the non-maintainability of the application due to alleged non-compliance with Section 42(4) of the Maharashtra Industrial Relations Act was not accepted. The court held that the employer failed to establish communication of the termination order, and thus the limitation period did not commence. The Labour Court is directed to proceed with the application on its merits and decide it preferably within six months.
